clue.text: Extra flexible in the mind

parts.note: flexible means supple, bending easily
something in the mind is mental, as in mental arithmetic

explanation.surface: Someone has a little more give in their thinking than most.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: an extra payment is an additional one, added to make up what was lacking.

clue.text: Student of central heating, operated by the sun outside

indicators.note: outside tells you the sun-powered word goes around the heating abbreviation

parts.note: a device operated by the sun is solar, as in solar panel
CH is the abbreviation for central heating in property adverts

explanation.surface: A trainee engineer studies radiators that run on sunshine from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal. 'Student of' reads as someone studying heating, but 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'central' picks no middle letters, it belongs to the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a learned pupil, or one holding a bursary, is a student.

clue.text: Block standard lines

parts.note: par is the standard or expected level, as in below par
RY is the abbreviation for railway, and railways are lines

explanation.surface: An order to obstruct the usual rows of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb in fencing or boxing: to ward off a blow is to block it.

clue.text: Slack feature of a table for 6?

definitions.note: 6 points to the answer at 6 down, a binder: this adjective describes the kind of binder whose pages can be taken out

parts.note: slack means loose, not tight
a leaf is the hinged or extra flap that extends a dining table

explanation.surface: A wobbly bit of furniture is laid for half a dozen diners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 is a cross-reference to the answer at 6 down, not a number of diners; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive example: a binder with removable pages is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Male assistance for this girl

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male on forms
aid means assistance or help

explanation.surface: A young woman is getting a helping hand from a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in old or poetic use: a maiden is an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Put up firearm — a right-minded type finds it worthless

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the weapon word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
a Tory, a British Conservative, is politically minded to the right

explanation.surface: A decent sort holsters a weapon, judging it useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns GUN into NUG. 'right-minded' pretends to mean sensible but points to the political right: a Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trifling and of no value or force is worthless.

clue.text: White of egg is mainly a binder

indicators.note: mainly means most of the egg-white word is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: albumen is the white of an egg

explanation.surface: A cook explains that egg white chiefly serves to hold a mixture together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' takes ALBUMEN without its final EN. A binder in the kitchen holds ingredients together; here it is a book that holds photographs or stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a book of blank pages holding photographs or stamps binds a collection together.

clue.text: It leads the Piggy-wig to make a short trunk call

parts.note: an elephant's trunk is its long nose, so a short one is just a nose
to ring someone is to call them by telephone

explanation.surface: Something guides a nursery-rhyme pig to a telephone for a brief long-distance chat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat' the Piggy-wig stood 'with a ring at the end of his nose'. A trunk call was a British long-distance telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary allusion: Lear's pig wore one in its snout, and such a hoop is how a farm animal is led.

clue.text: Toss and turn in new Herts hospital

indicators.note: new says the county abbreviation's letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps

explanation.surface: A patient spends a restless night on a ward just opened in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HERTS into THRES. Herts is the usual short form of Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to thrash about restlessly, as a sleepless person does in bed.

clue.text: Running furiously, holding racket, can be distressing

indicators.note: holding tells you the running word contains the noise word

parts.note: haring is running at great speed, like a hare
a racket is a noisy row or din

explanation.surface: Sprinting flat out across court with a tennis bat in hand takes its toll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal. The racket wants to be a tennis bat carried by a sprinting player; it is a din.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an experience that torments or deeply upsets is distressing.

clue.text: General stall

definitions.meaning: William, founder and first General of the Salvation Army
a covered stand at a market or fair

explanation.definitionFit: A surname and a common noun: the Salvation Army's founding General, and a covered market stand.

clue.text: Meanly disposed, they are not like priests

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of the adverb before it are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A stingy congregation shows none of the clergy's charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges MEANLY. 'Meanly disposed' reads as one phrase meaning ungenerous by nature, but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrast: these are the unordained members of a church, as opposed to its clergy.

clue.text: Running out of stock at an alarming rate

definitions.text: Running out of stock at an alarming rate

parts.words: Running out of stock at an alarming rate
parts.note: stock is livestock: a herd running out in panic at frightening speed, not a shop's shelves emptying

explanation.definitionFit: Punning description: frightened cattle bolting all together is a rush of livestock.

clue.text: Admiral yonder, at sea!

indicators.note: at sea means lost and confused, so the letters before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: A lookout points out a naval commander's ship on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges YONDER. George Rodney was the British admiral who won the Battle of the Saintes in 1782.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by name: George, an eighteenth-century British naval commander.

clue.text: Authorize agent to hand over commission

definitions.meaning: to depute someone to act as your representative
to pass a task or duty on to somebody else

explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: appointing a representative to act for you, and passing a task to someone else.

clue.text: Cold, uncooked seafood could be lobster

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
raw means uncooked
fish is seafood

explanation.surface: A chilled platter of sashimi might turn out to include shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the name is used for the spiny or rock lobster.

clue.text: Was he hurt after scrap and overwhelming defeat?

indicators.note: after says the reworked words follow the small-bit word

parts.note: a whit is a scrap, the tiniest bit

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so the two words before it are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fighter was injured following a brawl and a crushing loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' is the anagram signal for the first two words and 'after' gives the order. The scrap wants to be a fight; it is a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting sense: a contest in which the loser scores nothing or wins no game.

clue.text: Cold weather transport causes chaos in each city

indicators.note: chaos in the two words that follow means their letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Snowbound buses and trains bring every town to a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos in' rearranges EACH CITY. 'causes' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sailing craft on runners that travels over frozen lakes.

clue.text: One so-called type seen through red eyes?

definitions.text: One so-called type seen through red eyes?

parts.words: One so-called type seen through red eyes?
parts.note: red eyes are those of the 'Red Indian' of old Westerns, and this is the name he gave the white settler he saw

explanation.definitionFit: Allusion to Westerns: the name fictional Native Americans give a white person.

clue.text: General order we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for an arrangement is to be listened to, not read

parts.note: a pattern is an order or regular arrangement

explanation.surface: A command to the whole company reaches our ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear': PATTERN, in British speech with a silent R, sounds like the surname of George Patton, the American Second World War commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by name: George, the American tank commander of the Second World War.

clue.text: Meddle with index, for example

definitions.meaning: to touch or handle something you should leave alone
the index is the digit next to the thumb, one of four on a hand

explanation.definitionFit: A verb and a noun: handling something you should not, and a digit of the hand such as the pointing one.

clue.text: Language of upright type attending church

indicators.note: attending means the type word is accompanied by, and so stands beside, the church letters

parts.note: roman is the printer's name for upright type, as opposed to italic
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: The way a morally sound person talks at a Sunday service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attending' sets ROMAN beside CE. The upright type is printing, not a virtuous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example as an adjective or noun: French, Spanish and Italian belong to this family descended from Latin.

clue.text: Look after young lady of Riga's mount — it's brilliant

indicators.note: after says the looking word follows the limerick animal

parts.note: in the limerick, the young lady of Riga smiled as she rode on a tiger
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone minds a Latvian girl's splendid horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' gives the order of the two parts. The limerick runs: 'There was a young lady of Riga, who smiled as she rode on a tiger'; they returned with the lady inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a golden-brown gemstone with a shimmering band of light is a brilliant.

clue.text: Field variety

definitions.meaning: the scope or area that something covers
an assortment or selection of different things

explanation.definitionFit: Two noun senses: the scope something covers, and an assortment of different things.

clue.text: Hold up a ship and keep quiet

definitions.meaning: to leave a sailing vessel motionless for want of wind
split in two after the second letter, the entry is an instruction to stay tranquil

explanation.surface: Pirates seize a vessel and tell the crew not to make a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb and a spaced-out phrase: leaving a sailing vessel windless, and an instruction to stay tranquil.

clue.text: It takes so long to finish in a university

indicators.note: in places the ending word inside the two letters that follow it

parts.note: to die is to finish, to come to an end

explanation.surface: A degree course drags on for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DIE inside A U. 'so long' reads as a length of time but is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a farewell: both are ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Credit article reveals extent of catch

parts.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in the paper on borrowing shows how big the snag is.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran was the British measure for a landing of fresh herring, about 37 gallons; the catch is fish, not a snag.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical sense: an old measure of the quantity of herring landed.

clue.text: Decimal recurring again and again

definitions.meaning: decimal means based on the number after nine, which two short words can say

explanation.surface: A fraction whose digits repeat for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaced-out phrase and an adverb: based on the number after nine, and frequently.

clue.text: Pink in saloon race

parts.note: a saloon is the British name for a closed car with a separate boot, a sedan
a nation is a race or people

explanation.surface: A rosy-coloured entrant in a contest for family cars.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British word for a sedan car. Pink is the flower name, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical kinship: pinks are the Dianthus flowers, of which this is the best-known garden kind.

clue.text: Fox's followers assemble here

parts.note: Fox is George Fox, founder of the Quakers, so his followers are Friends gathering for worship, not hounds and huntsmen

explanation.definitionFit: Religious allusion: Quakers, whose founder was George Fox, worship in a building of this name.
